tickets.recommended_action: Rotating equipment specialist today: diagnose NDE vibration, set operating/repair disposition; correct per findings and verify vibration against approved limits. impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of the sole gas export compressor has a severe operational consequence: platform recycle and production reduction within an hour, with no spare or workaround. This supports 7–8, not an invented extreme accident consequence.

tickets.summary: PSV-1310 outlet hissing and hydrocarbon smell below set pressure suggest passing, raising doubt about V-1201 overpressure protection; relief capability and deviation status remain unverified.
tickets.recommended_action: Integrity engineer to set operating/repair disposition and regulatory deadline; inspect PSV and repair if passing is confirmed. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Confirm passing; pop/seat test after repair. Check gas levels and personnel exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Audible hissing and hydrocarbon smell below set pressure support an advanced leakage precursor and elevated near-term concern. The assessed function is V-1201 overpressure protection; passing is suspected, not proof that required relief capability has failed.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of the valve's overpressure-protection function would expose the first-stage production separator to a major-accident pressure-containment hazard. No redundant relief device is credited. This supports severe impact, but supplied evidence does not establish an extreme consequence magnitude.

tickets.summary: FW-8102 failed first start, then started on attempt 2 after about 8 s cranking and ran normally at rated pressure; batteries were 22.8 V at rest. Reliable on-demand firewater is compromised, with FW-8101 delivery also in doubt.
tickets.recommended_action: Mechanical/fire-protection engineers to approve findings-based repair and operating disposition; retain weekly tests. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Test batteries, charger and starting air. Retest first-start and rated pressure. Verify A duty flow/pressure capability.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Starting on demand is the assessed pump function. The first attempt failed during the weekly test; the successful second attempt after about eight seconds of cranking and subsequent normal running at rated discharge pressure do not erase that failure. Battery voltage was 22.8 V at rest, not during cranking. The cause and sustained restoration remain unresolved.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure to start removes this pump's on-demand firewater contribution, creating severe fire-protection exposure. Full N+1 credit is unsupported: the explicitly linked partner subsequently started correctly on 17 June but delivered 9.2 barg against 11 barg design, with flow unmeasured. This does not prove partner unavailability or total firewater failure. Both pumps being unavailable would require production shutdown; present combined capacity remains unknown.

tickets.summary: PL-1002 window 2 near the low-point drain has CUI wall loss to 6.2 mm versus 7.4 mm minimum on a live full-wellhead-pressure line, risking hydrocarbon release; adjacent windows are within tolerance.
tickets.recommended_action: Integrity engineer to set operating/repair disposition; repair as approved and renew wet insulation/weatherproofing; verify >=7.4 mm and pressure integrity. Map CUI/rate; verify repairs and line state. Check personnel exposure and release paths.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is pressure containment by the flowline. Thickness below the stated minimum, heavy scaling and saturated insulation establish advanced degradation supporting the 7–8 band. Adjacent acceptable windows limit the demonstrated extent, not the local damage. Neither imminent rupture nor actual containment loss is established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of pressure containment could release hydrocarbons at full wellhead pressure, creating credible serious personnel and major-accident exposure. No redundancy is stated. This supports severe consequence, but release magnitude, exposure and actual protective arrangements are insufficiently defined to justify an extreme band.

tickets.summary: FG-0455 failed to detect 50% LEL gas with two cylinders; two other heads responded, retaining compression-module gas detection but leaving the 2oo3 group without further failure margin.
tickets.recommended_action: Instrument engineer: repair or replace per diagnosis; approve operating disposition. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Verify current protection control alignment. Diagnose detector nonresponse. Retest head at 50% LEL and voted response.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is this detector head's hydrocarbon-gas response. Nonresponse on both successive gas challenges confirms its function loss; the other heads moderate impact, not this likelihood.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of this gas-detection channel moderately degrades protection against compression-module hydrocarbon gas hazards. Both remaining heads responded correctly, supporting retained voted capability, but another head failure would defeat the arrangement. This is not demonstrated total protection loss.

tickets.summary: CR-5001 hoist rope has 6 broken wires/lay versus 10 discard at the drum section for maximum radius. Other surveyed parts are satisfactory. Hoist failure risks dropped loads and loss of supply offloads, causing logistics problems within days.
tickets.recommended_action: Lifting engineer/surveyor to inspect full rope, restore lubrication, set operating/repair disposition and reinspection under lifting standard; verify rope below discard limits after work. Recount wires and establish progression. Check lift loads and personnel exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is supporting and hoisting loads through the main hoist rope. Six broken wires per lay remains below the stated discard count of ten, supporting limited degradation with margin. Poor lubrication warrants correction, but the single survey establishes neither progression nor operational function loss.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of the load-supporting hoist rope presents a credible dropped-load injury hazard. Crane unavailability also prevents supply boat offloads and creates logistics problems within days, with no registered redundancy. This supports a broad severe-consequence band, not an extreme consequence claim; actual loads and personnel exposure remain unknown.

tickets.summary: P-3305's third low-pressure trip this month interrupts wellhead inhibitor dosing (~10 days intermittent); loss need not stop production but risks downstream steel corrosion within weeks.
tickets.recommended_action: Maintenance engineer to direct repair of confirmed faults. Inspect diaphragm and low-pressure trip cause. Prove sustained injection at required duty. Integrity engineer: check dosing gaps and steel.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The required function is sustained corrosion-inhibitor injection to the wellhead manifold. impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of inhibitor delivery does not stop production, but starvation initiates downstream carbon-steel corrosion within weeks, creating delayed integrity consequences. No redundant pump is listed. Actual corrosion or containment loss is not established.

tickets.summary: Loose, wind-flapping cladding on K-3401's second-stage discharge line threatens to fall and injure personnel; the finding explicitly identifies no process concern.
tickets.recommended_action: Control the drop zone; inspect cladding and adjacent fixings. Have maintenance engineering specify reattachment or replacement; verify secure retention after repair. Check drop height, sheet mass and exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is retention of the discharge-line cladding against detachment, not gas compression. Loose lagging and wind-flapping cladding demonstrate advanced attachment degradation with continuing wind loading. Detachment is threatened but not established. The June 2 vibration observation is a separate mechanism and does not increase this finding's likelihood.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of cladding retention creates the explicitly identified dropped-object hazard, with credible serious personnel injury. This supports a broad severe-consequence band, although mass, drop height and personnel exposure require verification. The source excludes a process concern, so compressor trip and platform production loss are not attributed to this defect.

tickets.summary: DEL-8300's unlogged closed north-quadrant valve disabled wellhead deluge for an unknown duration; it is now reopened, but restored coverage remains unverified, with potential fire escalation and personnel exposure.
tickets.recommended_action: Fire protection engineer: investigate closure, fit status tag and approve disposition. Verify current protection control alignment. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Witness function test; close impairment only after pass. Review isolation history and exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is delivery of deluge water to the north quadrant. The closed branch isolation valve establishes loss of that function at discovery. Immediate reopening is confirmed, but restoration of delivery is not; the score does not assert that the valve remains closed.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of north-quadrant deluge removes fire-protection coverage above two producing wellheads, creating credible major-accident escalation and personnel consequences. No redundant arrangement is listed. This supports severe exposure, not an assumed total-platform loss or a precisely quantified injury outcome.

tickets.summary: Wet insulation and rust staining at V-1201's manway suggest hidden corrosion threatening first-stage pressure containment and potential hydrocarbon release; the vessel is thick-walled, but remaining thickness is unknown.
tickets.recommended_action: Integrity engineer: set service/repair disposition; correct damage and water ingress as found; verify integrity before dry insulation reinstatement. Check impairment/deviation records. Expose manway area; UT-map against limits. Check release inventory and personnel exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Wet insulation and rust staining are meaningful precursors to corrosion-related containment loss, supporting the 5–6 band. Hidden metal condition and progression are unmeasured; historical thick-wall margin does not establish current acceptance. The June 22 observation does not demonstrate leakage or failed containment. Earlier linked piping, relief-valve and transmitter findings do not establish vessel-shell damage.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of the first-stage separator pressure boundary presents credible severe hydrocarbon-release and personnel hazards, with no redundant vessel arrangement stated. This supports the severe-consequence band, not an extreme score based solely on SCE status. Release inventory, operating conditions and personnel exposure remain unknown. Linked relief and level-instrument observations are not proof of shell failure or effective mitigation.
